initial.prompt:
Use case: stylized-concept. Production candidate sprite atlas for a top-down pixel-art dungeon game.
Reference image 1 is the game's current wall models. Use ONLY the specified theme's DARK LOWER RECTANGULAR WALL FACE as the material/hue reference, lighten and desaturate it for the floor. Do not copy wall caps, brick arrangements, studs, 3D shapes or black grooves.
Reference images 2 and 3 are floor screenshots: use their restrained square-tile design language, sparse pixel wear and quiet flat surface. Do not recreate the screenshots or their blurry low resolution.
Create EXACTLY TEN square floor-tile variants in ONE wide 5-column by 2-row atlas. Canvas aspect ratio exactly 5:2, target 2560x1024, square cells 512x512. NO margins, NO spacing, NO labels, NO display board, NO background outside the cells. Each cell is ONE fully opaque flat square floor slab seen directly from overhead, edges aligned to the cell. The atlas fills the entire image. All ten are designed for random adjacency, each covering exactly one 8x8 world-unit square, the same width as one wall module.
Pixel art must be authored with crisp flat pixel clusters, about 48x48 logical pixels per cell, scaled nearest-neighbor. Carefully restrained pixel details in the style of Soul Knight floor sprites. NO antialiasing, blur, photographic texture, gradients, dense granular noise, clouds, sparkles or shiny bevels. Same fine game art language as the reference walls, but much quieter and flatter because this is walkable ground.
BORDER CONTRACT: all ten tiles have the EXACT SAME thin continuous 1-logical-pixel border using the ONE specified border color on ALL FOUR edges, including corners. Never black. No thick frame, no doubled interior frame, no raised rim or beveled edge. Identical border width, identical color, straight rectangular outline, no chips cut into outer contour. This uniform border is an intentional quiet grout seam for any random pairing.
Interiors can vary slightly in value, all always visibly lighter than the wall's dark lower face. Keep 90-95% of each tile plain and calm. Ten distinct subtle variants: four nearly plain with different tiny irregular tonal patches; two with restrained off-center straight pixel scuffs; two with faint short hairline wear marks; two with a small flat material patch. Vary patch position and shape asymmetrically. NO repetitive icons, circular motifs, raised stones, holes, pits, foliage, puddles, large fractures, multiple slabs subdividing one tile, or large directional shading. No texture feature crosses the uniform border. No dramatic alternating checkerboard values. No rotation or perspective. The whole result must look like ten variants from ONE consistent game tileset.

THEME: UNDERWATER STONE TEMPLE, the LEFTMOST wall. Muted cool blue-gray stone. Lower wall median RGB38,50,59. Floor face base RGB103,112,118 (#677076), with modest variants +/-8. Every face is much lighter than the dark wall. Exact uniform edge color #53606A, RGB83,96,106. No yellow moss, no marble veins. Broad quiet stone color with sparse subtle angular pixel wear.
